results.title: B300 Rental Prices per GPU-Hour: Signed Contracts Since March 2026 · CCIR
highlights:
# B300 Contract Prices Since March

 Eleven B300 rental contracts signed since March show three-year rates up about 25%, from $3.39 to $4.23 per GPU-hour. On a three-year contract for 10,000 GPUs, that move is about $220 million.

...

## 01 What prices did

- → Three-year rates: $3.39 to $4.23 per GPU-hour, up about 25%
- → Five-year rates: $3.30 to $3.77 per GPU-hour, up about 14%
- → Same provider: $3.45 in March on a three-year tenor, $3.94 in July on a four-year tenor

 Since March, seven listed companies disclosed 11 B300 rental contracts in their filings. The contracts cover about 31,000 GPUs and about $4 billion of contract value. 

 We fit a trend line to the rates and weight each contract by its GPU count. Three-year rates rose from about $3.39 per GPU-hour in March to $4.23 in August. That is a rise of about 25%. Five-year rates rose from $3.30 to $3.77, or about 14%. Two large contracts set most of the five-year line. 

 One seller shows the rise inside its own book. Boost Run rented 1,280 B300s for three years at $3.45 in March. In July it rented 1,536 for four years at about $3.94, on the same GPU-only basis. The July contract is also a year longer.

...

## 02 The move in dollars

- → 10,000 GPUs, three years: about $220 million
- → 10,000 GPUs, five years: about $200 million

 These contracts range from 128 to 9,200 GPUs. On a three-year contract for 10,000 B300s, the move from the March rate to the August rate is about $220 million. On a five-year contract for 10,000 GPUs, it is about $200 million. Both figures come from the trend lines in section 1.

results.title: What GPU Supply Shortage Means for CSPs
highlights:
Booking GPU capacity right now is a bit like calling the hottest restaurant in town. The reservation book is full into 2028, and the biggest party at the door just had two more people show up. AWS plans to deploy another two million Nvidia GPUs across 2027 and 2028, on top of an earlier commitment of more than one million. Nobody in the alternative Cloud world is shocked by the appetite, but the real question is what happens to everyone standing behind that party in line.

## The queue is real, and it’s long

Nvidia’s latest earnings call made the situation plain: supply, rather than demand, is what’s holding growth back, and the company doesn’t expect that to change overnight. It said supply commitments jumped from $119 billion to $279 billion in a single quarter, warning that shortages stretch from memory and silicon vendors to the suppliers building AI data centers.. Meanwhile, the hyperscalers and fast-growing GPU specialists such as CoreWeave and Nebius are scaling at a pace few others can match.

When supply is tight, allocation tends to follow scale. Big buyers place big, long-dated orders and get served first, which leaves smaller providers facing longer lead times, less predictable deliveries, and less room to negotiate.

...

The AI build-out is also pulling on memory and storage supply across the wider server market, and the effects show up well beyond the accelerator racks. Hosting providers including Hetzner and OVHcloud have raised prices this year, pointing to rising hardware costs and limited component availability. Even a provider that never sells a single GPU is feeling this in its refresh cycle and its margins.

For the sector as a whole, that adds up to a period of infrastructure inflation. Hardware costs more and takes longer to arrive, and every provider has to decide how much of that to absorb and how much to pass on. Those are uncomfortable conversations at renewal time; but the cause is easy to explain, which helps.

...

Here’s the more encouraging angle. When hyperscaler capacity is stretched and largely pre-booked, customers who can’t get what they need, or can’t stomach the price, start looking elsewhere. Alternative Cloud providers are well placed to capture that demand, especially when they offer what the big platforms find harder to deliver at scale: smaller, more flexible deployments, regional data residency, hands-on support, and simpler pricing.

It also helps that plenty of AI work doesn’t need the newest silicon. Inference, fine-tuning, and smaller task-specific models often run happily on previous-generation hardware, so not every customer needs the latest chip. The GPU shortage rewards providers who match the workload to the right hardware.

...

Zoom out and the shortage is reshaping the structure of the market. Capacity is concentrating with the biggest buyers, which widens the gap between providers ... It also sharpens the case for regional and sovereign options, where data location and local control matter as much as raw performance.

...

Nobody can conjure GPUs out of thin air, but plenty is within a provider’s control:

• Plan procurement earlier. Longer lead times call for forecasting further ahead and building relationships with more than one supplier.

• Get more from what you have. Scheduling, multi-tenancy, and better utilization stretch every GPU further.

• Right-size the offer. Reserve top-end hardware for the workloads that need it and steer the rest toward alternatives.

• Revisit pricing and contract terms. Build in ways to handle component cost swings so they don’t land entirely on your margin.

• Sort out power and cooling early. These often take longer to arrange than the hardware itself.

• Be straight with customers. Clear timelines build more trust than optimistic ones.

results.title: Рынок GPU в России: аренда H100 и дефицит мощностей
highlights:
На Хабре вышел разбор рынка вычислений в России, Казахстане и Беларуси. Автор оценил дефицит мощностей к 2030 году в 3 ГВт, привёл прайсы на аренду H100 от 342 ₽ в час и посчитал полную стоимость серого железа с наценками до 100%.

...

## Три слоя дефицита

Первый слой — мощности. К российским сетям подключено порядка 5 ГВт ЦОДов, из них 2,7 ГВт приходится на майнинг. Без майнинга — около 2 ГВт на всю страну. Для сравнения: у CoreWeave 1,5 ГВт активных мощностей, а контракты требуют 8 ГВт к 2030 году.

Самый амбициозный российский проект — ЦОД Cloud.ru в Подмосковье на ~60 МВт с перспективой до 100 МВт, ввод в 2026 году. Яндекс запустил крупнейший частный ЦОД страны во Владимирской области — около 100 МВт, больше 30 млрд рублей инвестиций. Сбалансированный дефицит рынка к 2030 году автор оценивает в ~3 ГВт.

Второй слой — чипы. NVIDIA поставляется только через параллельный импорт с наценкой от паритета до 2,5 раз. Отечественных ускорителей для обучения нет — есть заявленные проекты инференс-чипов (Яндекс, Сбер, МТС) и нишевые нейропроцессоры НТЦ «Модуль». Реальный парк страны: кластер Сбера на ~9000 A100 и ~6 тысяч GPU у Яндекса.

Третий слой — память. Триополия Samsung, SK Hynix и Micron перебросила мощности на HBM для GPU. Дефицит, по словам председателя SK Hynix, продлится до 2030 года, а 2027-й обещает стать худшим годом предложения в истории отрасли.

## Стоимость серого железа

H100 на параллельном импорте стоит дороже американского прайса. По дилерским прайсам сентября карта 80 ГБ идёт за 2,65–3,86 млн ₽ — от паритета с американским (около $31 тыс.) до полутора раз. На топовых поколениях наценка доходила до 2,5 раз.

Официальной гарантии NVIDIA нет — только реселлерская на 3–12 месяцев или никакой. Лицензий NVIDIA AI Enterprise тоже нет, а с ними исчезают сертифицированные драйверы и enterprise-поддержка. Автор рекомендует закладывать к цене карточки ещё 30–100% и только получившуюся сумму сравнивать с арендой.

Публичные прайсы собраны 20–21 сентября. Минимальная ставка за час H100 — от ~342 ₽ (immers.cloud) и ~352 ₽ (Intelion). Cloud.ru сдаёт блок 5xH100 от 2250 ₽/час — по 450 ₽ за карту. Верх рыночного диапазона — до ~470 ₽/час. Глобальная аренда H100 стоит от ~$1,5 на дисконтных маркетплейсах до ~$7 у премиальных провайдеров, медиана — около $3,3 в час.

...

Автор приводит расчёт Beeline Cloud для H100 на горизонте пяти лет: аренда стоит 920 ₽ за час, свой сервер — 5 млн разово плюс электричество, около 330 ₽ за каждый час работы. Порог рентабельности покупки — 25–30 тысяч часов реальной занятости за пять лет, то есть карта должна работать больше половины времени.

При круглосуточной загрузке аренда за пять лет съедает около 40 млн, свой вариант — около 30 млн. С поправкой на старение железа (час карты дешевеет на 15–20% в год) реальная окупаемость растягивается до 5–8 лет.

Автор также отмечает, что лизинговые проценты начисляются на остаток долга, а не на цену карты. Ключевая ставка вернулась к 14% с июля 2026 года. При аренде в 500–600 ₽/час арендованный час дороже своего всего на 170–270 ₽ с учётом электроэнергии.

results.title: NovaCore — Bare Metal GPU Superclusters
highlights:
# B200 and B300 Prices Hit All-Time Highs as Demand Outpaces Blackwell Supply

NovaCore Team September 24, 2026

The Blackwell era was supposed to ease GPU pricing pressure. Instead, the opposite has happened: spot and contract rates for B200 and B300 capacity have climbed to all-time highs, with B300 hourly pricing up more than 40% since its January launch and B200 rates following close behind.

For teams planning training runs or scaling inference fleets in the next two quarters, the dynamics behind this matter more than the headline numbers.

...

Three forces are compounding at once.

Reasoning models changed the demand curve. Inference-heavy reasoning workloads consume far more compute per query than classic chat-style serving. The B300's 288GB of HBM3e makes it the natural home for long-context reasoning inference, and buyers have responded. Capacity that was expected to serve training demand is being absorbed by inference fleets instead.

Rubin anticipation froze the secondary market. With Rubin on the horizon, large holders of Blackwell allocation are locking in long-term contracts rather than releasing capacity to spot markets. Less spot supply means spot prices clear higher — and contract pricing follows.

HBM remains the hard ceiling. CoWoS packaging capacity has expanded, but HBM3e output is still the binding constraint on B300 production. Every GB300 NVL72 rack ships with over 20TB of HBM, and memory suppliers are sold out through mid-2027.

## The numbers

- B300 hourly rates on major marketplaces are up 40%+ from January launch pricing
- B200 spot pricing has recovered past its 2025 peak, despite a full year of production ramp
- Multi-year reserved contracts for GB300 NVL72 racks are closing at premiums to list that would have been unthinkable during the H100 glut of early 2025
- H200 pricing, by contrast, has stayed flat — the squeeze is specific to Blackwell

...

If you need Blackwell capacity in the next six months, reserve now. The spot market is the most expensive way to access B200/B300 today, and the premium is widening. Reserved capacity at today's contract rates will look cheap by Q1 2027 if current trends hold.

...

Geography matters more than ever. Pricing pressure is most acute in U.S. regions. Capacity in India and the Middle East — where new data center buildouts are coming online faster than local demand is absorbing them — is clearing at meaningful discounts to U.S. rates for identical hardware.

results.title: Viewpoint: The halving of LLM token prices does not signal a weakening in AI demand; the GPU computing power rental market remains robust with strong demand. - Lookonchain - Looking for smartmoney onchain
highlights: Professional data firm Silicon Data published a report noting that the market has recently frequently cited its LLM Token Index as a basis for bearish bets on AI trading, but the index’s decline does not signal a weakening of AI demand or model-layer profits. Silicon Data explained that its LLM Token Index measures the actual price paid per million tokens by API users in its sample — referred to as the "usage-weighted price" — rather than token volume or total spending. The index fell 52% from $2.07 on May 28 to $1 on September 21, but had risen 67% between January and its May peak, meaning price movements alone cannot serve as a direct indicator of AI industry sentiment. The firm pointed out that the recent index decline mainly reflects more tasks being allocated to cheaper, faster models, while AI labs continue rolling out additional mid-tier models. Since tokens do not fully represent AI capabilities, the index also cannot distinguish between model substitution and more efficient agent routing on its own. By contrast, the GPU computing power rental market still shows strong demand. Silicon Data’s data shows that rental prices for H200 GPUs at non-hyperscale cloud providers rose from an average of $2.87 in June to $3.29 currently, hitting $3.32 on September 19; B200 GPUs now trade at $5.76, up 7% year-over-year and 31% year-to-date; B300 GPUs have risen 44% since their launch at the end of April. Silicon Data believes that with the large-scale adoption of agents, the vast majority of tokens in the future will likely come from cheap, fast models, so token prices can continue to decline while total token volume still grows significantly. The firm added that truly high-value tasks will likely remain concentrated on frontier models, and the widespread adoption of AI means demand for computing power could be "more, not less".
